facts.text: ISO 3450 and ISO 10265 specify earth-moving machine brake performance and testing: ISO 3450 covers wheeled and fast rubber-tracked machines, while ISO 10265 covers slow crawler machines.
facts.quote: ISO 3450 and ISO 10265 are the standards that say how well the brakes of an earth-moving machine must work and how to test them, ISO 3450 for wheeled and fast rubber-tracked machines and ISO 10265 for slow crawler machines.

facts.text: ISO 3450:2011, edition 4, confirmed in 2022, specifies minimum service, secondary and parking brake performance and tests for wheeled earth-moving machines and rubber-tracked machines with a top speed of at least 20 km/h.
facts.quote: ISO 3450:2011 (edition 4, confirmed 2022) specifies minimum service, secondary and parking brake performance and tests for wheeled earth-moving machines and rubber-tracked machines with a top speed of 20 km/h or more

facts.text: ISO 3450 covers purpose-built underground mining machines only through an annex of modifications.
facts.quote: purpose-built underground mining machines are covered only by an annex of modifications

facts.text: ISO 10265:2008, confirmed in 2025, covers crawler machines at 20 km/h or less.
facts.quote: ISO 10265:2008 (confirmed 2025) covers crawler machines at 20 km/h or less

facts.text: Based on a secondary technical article, the booklet reports that ISO 3450 tests brakes at 32 km/h or 80 percent of maximum speed and sets formula-based stopping limits by machine type.
facts.quote: From a secondary technical article, the booklet reports that ISO 3450 tests at 32 km/h or 80 percent of maximum speed and sets formula-based stopping limits by machine type

facts.text: The booklet's secondary-article example of an ISO 3450 stopping limit for rigid and articulated dumpers under 32 t is v^2 / 44 + 0.1 (32 - v), with test speed v in km/h and stopping distance in meters.
facts.quote: for example `v^2 / 44 + 0.1 (32 - v)` for rigid and articulated dumpers under 32 t, where v is the test speed in km/h and the result is in meters

facts.text: The ISO 3450 stopping-limit formulas reported from a secondary technical article should be checked against the standard.
facts.quote: these formulas should be checked against the standard

facts.text: Stopping distance runs from the start of brake-control actuation to standstill, including brake-system response time but excluding operator reaction time.
facts.quote: stopping distance runs from the start of brake-control actuation to standstill, so it includes brake-system response time but excludes operator reaction time

facts.text: ISO 3450 and ISO 10265 braking tests are physical tests; the booklet found no simulation wording in these standards.
facts.quote: These are physical tests; no simulation wording was found

facts.text: Neither ISO 3450 nor ISO 10265 specifies a number of calibration stops that would establish trust in a braking model across 100 or more site types.
facts.quote: neither standard gives a number of calibration stops that would let a braking model be trusted across 100 or more site types

facts.text: ISO 17757 requires autonomous machines to pass the same physical braking tests in manual and autonomous mode.
facts.quote: ISO 17757 requires autonomous machines to pass the same physical braking tests in manual and autonomous mode

facts.text: ISO 21815-3's CxS distance, the required collision-system distance, is based on real stopping distance; ISO 3450 brake data for each machine model therefore feeds the collision-avoidance calculation.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3's CxS distance (its required collision-system distance) is built on real stopping distance, so ISO 3450 brake data per machine model is an input to the collision-avoidance calculation

facts.text: Passing ISO 3450 does not demonstrate perception performance.
facts.quote: Passing ISO 3450 proves nothing about perception

facts.text: Excellent perception cannot compensate for a brake plant that fails its own stopping requirements.
facts.quote: excellent perception cannot rescue a brake plant that fails its own stopping requirements

facts.text: On gravel, mud, ice and grades of 10 percent or more, ISO 3450 is more relevant to the braking program than an imported passenger-car deceleration target.
facts.quote: on gravel, mud, ice and grades of 10 percent or more, ISO 3450 is more relevant than any imported passenger-car deceleration target
